original_value: In this work, we present a processing chain for landscape pattern and ecological security status assessment and prediction based on cellular automata Markov (CA-Markov) and pressure status response pattern (PSRP) models using remotely sensed data (RSD) captured in 1986, 1996, 2006, 2016, and RSD simulated in 2026 over Zhengzhou city, Henan province, China. Three major findings can be withdrawn through the experiments. First, there is a significant changing of landscape type area, especially for building land. The area of building land is up to more than 5%, from 1986 to 2016. Secondly, the heterogeneity of landscape is increasing, and the diversity of landscape is becoming more and more diversifying and complex. Third, the changing trend of ecological security of Zhengzhou city shaped as decreasing and increasing gradually during the last 40 years. While the ecological security status, nowadays, appeared to a good trend by contrast of the previous stages. The predicted results with CA-Markov model show that the level of ecological security is still in moderate and has a trend of moving toward to the center in 2026.

result.paraphrase: This study proposes a workflow for assessing and forecasting landscape patterns and ecological security status using cellular automata Markov (CA-Markov) and pressure status response pattern (PSRP) models, based on remotely sensed data (RSD) from 1986, 1996, 2006, and 2016, plus simulated RSD for 2026 in Zhengzhou, Henan Province, China. The experiments yield three main findings. First, landscape area has changed markedly, especially for built-up land, whose area increased by more than 5% from 1986 to 2016. Second, landscape heterogeneity has risen, making landscape diversity increasingly varied and complex. Third, Zhengzhou’s ecological security has shown a declining then gradually rising trend over the past 40 years, and its current status appears better than in earlier stages. CA-Markov predictions indicate that ecological security will remain at a moderate level in 2026 and will tend to move toward the center.
